item.title: European Energy Sector Updates Cybersecurity Strategies to Address AI-Driven Grid Threats
item.description:
European Energy Sector Updates Cybersecurity Strategies to Address AI-Driven Grid Threats

Experts gathering at the 9th Cybersecurity Forum in Brussels are warning that the European energy sector must close the gap between rapidly evolving cyber threats and practical response capabilities. The forum addresses new risks created by geopolitical attacks, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into malicious operations, and the growth of connected energy technologies.

🔍 Overview

The event follows the release of ENISA’s Threat Landscape 2026, which analyzed 8,257 cyber incidents from 2025. The report found that attackers are increasingly incorporating AI into their operations while claims of intrusions related to operational technology (OT)—the systems used to control physical equipment and industrial processes—have increased.

🧩 How it works

The sector is observing how AI can be used as both a tool for attackers and a critical component of grid defense.

Entity AI and Cybersecurity Application
NPC Ukrenergo Uses AI to help cybersecurity teams react faster, identify gaps, support staff, and assist with reporting
Malicious Actors Incorporate AI into operations to shape geopolitical cyber activity and target OT systems
ENCS Identifies vulnerabilities in connected devices that use unauthenticated control protocols

⚙️ Key details

Recent real-world attacks provide a baseline for what grid cyber resilience requires in practice:

  • Poland (December 2025): A coordinated attack targeted wind and solar farms and a combined heat and power plant. Although electricity generation continued, attackers disrupted communications and gained access levels that could have enabled further disruption.
  • Ukraine: NPC Ukrenergo is sharing lessons on maintaining a grid under sustained attack, emphasizing the challenge of keeping specialist cybersecurity expertise when skilled teams are difficult to rebuild.
  • Connected Device Risks: ENCS researchers demonstrated that attackers can use compromised everyday devices, such as routers or cameras, to communicate with residential solar inverters or home batteries that lack command authentication.

💡 Why it matters

The expansion of high-power IoT devices creates a risk where manipulating thousands of units simultaneously could cause sudden changes in generation or demand, potentially leading to wider grid disturbances. Harm van den Brink, a security researcher at ENCS, noted that vulnerabilities in these devices have already been exploited and requires a shift toward independent security testing and manufacturer-led vulnerability management. Dimitra Liveri of ENISA stated that the challenge requires moving from protecting individual systems to optimizing the entire ecosystem for resilience.

#Cybersecurity #ArtificialIntelligence #EnergyGrid #GridResilience #EU

Source: E.DSO, EE-ISAC, ENCS and ENISA 9th Cybersecurity Forum – Press Release | E.DSO

item.title: EU Parliament Pushes for Global AI Governance Treaty and New Safeguards
item.description:
EU Parliament Pushes for Global AI Governance Treaty and New Safeguards

European lawmakers on the Parliament’s Constitutional Affairs Committee (AFCO) have approved a report that asks Brussels to spearhead a global AI agreement, tighten safeguards against election manipulation, and create a budget‑neutral AI Observatory inside the European Parliament.

🔍 Overview

  • The AFCO report calls for an international AI‑governance treaty modelled on nuclear non‑proliferation arrangements.
  • It was backed by 21 votes in favour, three against and no abstentions.
  • The proposal argues that AI’s scale, speed and cross‑border impact justify a dedicated global convention or treaty.

📜 Report Highlights

  • Human oversight: AI used by EU institutions must remain under human control, even though the technology can help identify legal inconsistencies.
  • Election safeguards: Stronger action is proposed against deepfakes, micro‑targeting and voter manipulation, addressing the risk of AI influencing elections.
  • Fundamental‑rights updates: The report urges amendments to the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights to protect personal identity and likeness, ensure algorithmic transparency, guarantee digital self‑determination and prevent algorithmic discrimination.
  • AI Observatory: A new European Parliament AI Observatory would provide technical and analytical support to parliamentary committees, be budget‑neutral and built from existing expertise, without regulatory or enforcement powers.

🌐 Global AI Governance Proposal

  • The report likens AI to transformative technologies such as nuclear technology, suggesting a similar international regime.
  • It emphasizes that fragmented European electoral frameworks are ill‑suited to counter AI‑driven misinformation, reinforcing the need for coordinated global rules.

🛡️ Safeguards & Human Oversight

  • Deepfake & micro‑targeting controls: Targeted measures against synthetic media and manipulative political advertising.
  • Human‑in‑the‑loop requirement: AI can assist law‑making but must not replace human responsibility.

🏛️ AI Observatory Details

  • Purpose: Deliver technical and analytical assistance to parliamentary committees.
  • Funding: Designed to be budget‑neutral, leveraging existing parliamentary expertise.
  • Authority: No regulatory or enforcement powers are granted.

📅 Next Steps

  • The report is slated for debate before the full Parliament during the 19 – 22 October plenary session.
  • It builds on the March‑approved AI Convention that placed fundamental rights, democracy and the rule of law at the centre of AI governance, moving the agenda a step further.

💡 Why It Matters

  • By positioning the EU as a leader in global AI governance, the proposal seeks to shape international standards that match AI’s rapid, cross‑border influence.
  • Strengthening election safeguards and human oversight aims to protect democratic accountability and fundamental values in the AI era.
  • The AI Observatory could enhance parliamentary scrutiny without creating new regulatory burdens.

#EU #AIRegulation #GlobalAI #Democracy

Source: Should AI be governed like nuclear technology? EU lawmakers call for global rules - EU Perspectives

item.title: ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox designated as Very Large Online Platforms under EU DSA
item.description:
ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox designated as Very Large Online Platforms under EU DSA

The European Commission has designated ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms under the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA), subjecting them to stricter accountability and transparency rules.

🔍 Overview

ChatGPT is now classified as a Very Large Online Search Engine under the DSA, while Reddit and Roblox are designated as Very Large Online Platforms. These designations apply to services with at least 45 million average monthly users in the EU.

⚙️ Key details

  • Platforms must mitigate risks related to minors, user mental health, and the spread of illegal content.
  • Restrictions include banning targeted ads to minors and prohibiting the use of sensitive personal data (e.g., sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, or political beliefs) for ad targeting.
  • Platforms must provide greater transparency about their recommendation algorithms.

📅 Compliance timeline

ChatGPT, Reddit, and Roblox have until the end of December 2026 to comply with the DSA rules.

💡 Why it matters

Henna Virkkunen, EU executive vice-president for tech sovereignty, security and democracy, stated: “These new designations mean that ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox will now be held to a higher standard of scrutiny and accountability in the European Union, in line with their large impact on our citizens and society.”

#DSA #EU #ChatGPT #Reddit #Roblox #OnlinePlatforms

Source: ChatGPT to face tougher regulation in the EU
